speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for coming in. To understand the cause of your gait and limb ataxia, could you tell me exactly how long you have been experiencing these balance issues and if they have been getting worse?

Have you noticed any specific symptoms like double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your arms or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying. You mentioned feeling particularly clumsy on the right side; are these symptoms constant, or do they get worse when you walk in the dark? Also, have you experienced any changes in your vision, such as double vision, or any numbness/tingling in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to Natalizumab use.

This is a critical finding given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab. The combination of gait/limb ataxia (worse on the right) and the specific medication you are taking is highly suspicious for PML, an opportunistic brain infection.

I need to confirm your recent neurologic status and schedule urgent imaging.
1. Have you noticed any new areas of weakness, numbness, or changes in your vision or speech in the last few weeks?
2. When was your last MRI of the brain?
3. REQUEST TEST: JC Virus antibody status (CSF).
4. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_with_contrast.
